newsitem.title: PARAGUAY: Paraguay's ex-army chief cleared of rebellion charge.
newsitem.headline: Paraguay's ex-army chief cleared of rebellion charge.

text.p: A Paraguayan appeals court on Thursday found former army chief Lino Oviedo innocent of charges of attempted rebellion against the government.
The charges arose from the April 22 incident in which Oviedo holed himself up in his barracks resisting his discharge ordered by President Juan Carlos Wasmosy.

The standoff caused fears of a military coup. The crisis ended after the president appeared to back down by offering Oviedo the post of defense minister. But Wasmosy had fooled the general, who was stripped of his rank and put on trial.
In a ruling broadcast on radio, the court declared the charges against Oviedo should be dropped as he had eventually followed Wasmosy's orders and stood down as army chief.
Oviedo, who wants to run for president, denied he tried to overthrow Wasmosy in April.

In another development on Thursday, Wasmosy discharged 115 army officers on disciplinary charges. Wasmosy told reporters that the army purge had nothing to do with the events in April. But those dismissed had all added their signatures to a declaration that they had not been ordered by Oviedo to rebel.
